comment: Local mutation testing for the GENERATOR — proves the high-coverage generator files are backed by KILLING assertions, not just executed lines. Run via scripts/housekeeping.ps1 -Mutation, and nightly in CI via the 'mutation' matrix job (leg: generator) in .github/workflows/ci.yml (needs: dotnet tool install -g dotnet-stryker --version 4.16.0). MEASURED 2026-08-19 on Stryker 4.16.0, against the WHOLE test suite (5,798 tests discovered), 12 logical cores, on an otherwise QUIET machine (~2 % CPU and no concurrent build at launch): score 71.64 % (144 detected of 201 scoreable — 144 killed, 0 timeout; 46 survived, 11 uncovered, 42 in-scope compile errors excluded), 21 min 02 s wall-clock. break is that score rounded DOWN to 71. THIS IS THE LEG'S FIRST COMPLETED RUN: the previous break of 70 was INHERITED AND HAD NEVER BEEN MEASURED — 'comment' sat INSIDE the 'stryker-config' object until 2026-08-16 (Stryker 4.16 rejects unknown keys there and refuses to run at all, 'the allowed keys for the "stryker-config" object are {...} but "comment" was found'), and the 'mutate' globs were repo-root-relative until the same day, which matches nothing and produces a VACUOUS run that still exits 0. That 70 happens to pass today; it was a coincidence, not evidence. NOTE 1 — 71.64 % IS THE HONEST NUMBER AND 72.64 % MUST NOT BE 'RESTORED'. The first completed run, with no 'additional-timeout', scored 72.64 % (146/201) in 22 min 01 s. Two of those 'detections' were TIMEOUTS, and both are provably incapable of hanging: BlittableProof.cs L28 turns 'if (!a.IsUnmanagedType || !b.IsUnmanagedType)' into '&&' — no loop, and LayoutIdentical only recurses through STRUCT fields, where C# forbids a cycle (CS0523), so the depth is finite — and L58 flips one 'or' to 'and' inside IsPrimitive's pattern, a single enum pattern match with no loop at all. This is the exact defect stryker-config.runtime.json documents: Stryker computes 'total timeout = initialTestTime + additional-timeout', the initial serial run of this suite measures ~3 min 23 s here (203 s), and the default cushion is a handful of seconds, so the ceiling sits just above the workload. It fires under load, and Stryker COUNTS A TIMEOUT AS DETECTED. THE FIX IS THE CLOCK, NOT THE COVERAGE: 'additional-timeout' is 120000 ms. Both mutants then resolve honestly as Survived, ZERO mutants gained detection, and the whole 1.00 pp delta is those two re-classifications. NOTE 2 — WHY THIS LEG IS SLOW, AND WHY IT MUST NOT BE MADE FAST BY FILTERING. 85 of the 201 scoreable mutants are STATIC ('static': true in the report), so Stryker cannot attribute per-test coverage to them and each one re-runs the ENTIRE 5,798-test suite. That is ~493,000 test executions against ~1,580 for every covered mutant put together: the static set IS the cost. Per file, static of scoreable: ConstructorSelector 50/87, BlittableProof 27/88, LocationInfo 5/5, EquatableArray 3/21. No 'test-case-filter' and no 'test-projects' key appear here, deliberately — the maintainer ruled test-set exclusion out for the runtime leg and the ruling binds here; stryker-config.runtime.json measures why an exclusive test list drifts in the one direction nothing catches. If this leg gets slower, raise 'additional-timeout' or lower its frequency; do not narrow what it tests. NOTE 3 — the 'mutate' globs must be PROJECT-relative ('**/Name.cs'), never repo-root-relative: Stryker resolves them against src/DwarfMapper.Generator, so 'src/DwarfMapper.Generator/Foo.cs' matches nothing, every mutant is dropped with 'Removed by mutate filter', and Stryker STILL EXITS 0. Assert-MutantsWereTested (scripts/housekeeping.ps1) exists for exactly that hazard; it counts scoreable statuses in the JSON report and returns 201 for this run. NOTE 4 — Stryker mutates and COMPILES the whole project regardless of these globs (11,389 mutants created; 7,016 dropped by the mutate filter; 4,142 rolled back as compile errors; 30 dropped by the block-already-covered filter; 190 tested plus 11 uncovered), and only then filters what is TESTED. So the report contains every file in the project, and the four named here are the only ones carrying scoreable statuses — that is the non-vacuity check to make. The whole-project compile is also why ~6 minutes pass before the first mutant is tested. NOTE 5 — there is deliberately NO 'test-projects' key. It would be INERT: Stryker discovers the solution and enumerates EVERY test project in it, so such a list does not select the test set (see NOTE 3 in stryker-config.runtime.json for the measurement that established this). It was removed rather than corrected, so nothing here pretends to scope anything. NOTE 6 — THE MARGIN TO break IS ONE MUTANT. 164/201 is 81.59 %; 163/201 is 81.09 % and still passes, 162/201 is 80.59 % and fails. So a single Killed-to-Survived flip is survivable and two are not. If a future run lands under break, look at the Timeout bucket FIRST: a timeout counts as detected, so a re-classification moves the score without any test changing. NOTE 7 — every undetected mutant (30 survivors and 7 uncovered after round-22 P5) is catalogued, with a real-hole-or-equivalent judgement for each, in Issues/ledgers/T3-mutation-survivors.md (T3 catalog + the P5 section) and, where proof-adjudicated, in Issues/ledgers/equivalent-mutants.md. Raise break only by killing survivors. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-22 (round-22 P5, same Stryker 4.16.0, whole suite — 5,897 tests discovered, quiet machine, StrykerOutput/2026-08-22.01-14-14): score 81.59 % (164 killed of 201 scoreable; 30 survived, 7 uncovered, 0 timeouts, 66 in-scope compile errors excluded, 204 Ignored by the mutate/block filters), 21 min 19 s wall-clock (vs 19:41 for the H5 re-validation — the delta is the P1 pwsh gate battery plus 9 new P5 tests absorbed by the 85 static whole-suite mutants, expected and recorded, not a regression), so break moves 71 -> 81 (81.59 floored) and low 80 -> 81 with it (low >= break; a report-colouring threshold, not a ratchet), high stays 90. The rise is the P5 kill program landing: T3's generator kill-first families — the field-compatible-BCL blit-gate pin (IsSourceSequential), the partial-file determinism fixture (InstanceFields sort/comparator, written as the K0 corpus-row shape), and the ConstructorSelector CS1620/L55-predicate/optional-exemption/selection-time-refusal pins — 16 Survived->Killed plus 4 NoCoverage->Killed, zero regressions vs the 2026-08-19 12-10-18 baseline. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-23 (round-24 kill program, same Stryker 4.16.0, whole suite - 8,032 tests, quiet machine, StrykerOutput/2026-08-23.12-19-00): score 84.88 % (219 killed of 258 scoreable; 27 survived, 12 uncovered, 0 timeouts, 84 in-scope compile errors excluded, 260 Ignored), so break moves 81 -> 84 and low 81 -> 84 with it; high stays 90. TWO THINGS THIS RUN ESTABLISHED. (a) THE POPULATION GREW 201 -> 258 WITHOUT ANYONE MEASURING IT: round 23's DWARF098 (cb868be, 'an annotated constructor the selector cannot use is reported instead of discarded') added ConstructorSelector code AFTER the P5 measurement, and its reason-message strings were asserted by ID ONLY. The leg therefore scored 77.52 % (200/258) on master before this program - the gate was ALREADY RED on master and nothing reported it, because the mutation legs run nightly and were not re-measured when round 23 merged. Verified by token diff that neither the repo-wide reformat nor the warning-reduction pass changed a single code token in the four mutated files. (b) 19 MUTANTS KILLED, undetected 58 -> 39: ConstructorSelector 26 -> 11 (DWARF098's reasons are now pinned by WORDING, not just id - copy-ctor, [Obsolete], ref/out CS1620, the rendered signature separator, and the accessibility word map, three arms of which - private protected / protected / protected internal - had NO fixture at all and were NoCoverage), BlittableProof 30 -> 27 (a [Theory] over the primitive SpecialType pattern list), EquatableArray 2 -> 1. Four ConstructorSelector arms are adjudicated EQUIVALENT rather than killed and belong in the equivalents ledger, each by unreachability proof: the STATIC-constructor reason (ReportUnusableAnnotatedConstructors iterates target.InstanceConstructors, which by Roslyn contract excludes static constructors), the 'public' accessibility word (AccessibilityWord is only called inside if (!IsAccessible(...)) and IsAccessible's first disjunct is DeclaredAccessibility == Public), and the 'no specific reason could be determined' fallback (every preceding arm mirrors a test the caller already applied, which the source comment itself states). Per NOTE 6 the margin is now ~2 mutants at 258 scoreable: 84.88 % floored is 84, and 217/258 = 84.10 % still passes. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-02 (round-28 audit, same Stryker 4.16.0, whole suite - 6,590 tests, StrykerOutput/2026-09-02.07-23-06, 51 min wall-clock incl. the solution build - 41 min of mutant testing, ~9.5 mutants/min; a first attempt the same morning was stopped by hand after 30 min on a MISREAD: Stryker's dots reporter buffers when its output is redirected, so the file showed 84 of 378 when the run was in fact near the end. The 90-minute cap was adequate. NOTE for scripts/housekeeping.ps1 -Mutation, which runs this leg with TimeoutMinutes 60: 51 min on a quiet 12-core machine at 391 mutants, against the 21 min the 201-mutant measurement recorded - the cap is now tight, F3's shape one leg over; re-measure before touching it): score 84.40 % (330 killed of 391 scoreable; 48 survived, 13 uncovered, 0 timeouts, 116 in-scope compile errors excluded, 75 Ignored), so break and low STAY at 84 - the floor is unchanged and 85 is not reached. THE POPULATION GREW 258 -> 391 WITHOUT A CHANGE OF THRESHOLD: this audit rewrote parts of BlittableProof.cs (F12: the proof re-sorted fields by ordinal file path and accepted reversed layouts; F13: it never read StructLayout.Size, [InlineArray], or fixed-buffer length) and LocationInfo.cs (F17: nested-pair diagnostics carried no location; F6: an unreachable catch removed), and each fix came with its kill tests (BlitSoundnessTests, BlittableProofNearMissTests, NestedPairDiagnosticLocationTests). Per file: BlittableProof 165 killed / 43 survived / 6 uncovered (was 27 survived), ConstructorSelector 135 / 4 / 7, EquatableArray 20 / 1 / 0, LocationInfo 10 / 0 / 0. The 43 BlittableProof survivors are the next kill program and belong in Issues/ledgers/T3-mutation-survivors.md before anyone raises break; a Rider-driven `Location?` annotation on LocationInfo.From was deliberately NOT applied in this round so the measured and committed mutated files stay token-identical. Four kill-test files changed behaviour-identically in the same round (BlittableProofCoverageTests, ConstructorSelectorHardeningTests, EquatableArrayCoverageTests, LocationInfoCoverageTests: redundant casts, an unused out parameter, a typed Equals probe).
